output.risk_rationale: As of 2026-10-20, risk is high: Spirit Airlines, LLC is a Chapter 11 debtor, and all flights were cancelled on May 2, 2026 after additional funding could not be obtained (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1498710/000095010326006723/dp246246_ex9901.htm). Fitch subsequently affirmed its issuer rating at D and withdrew it following the decision to cease operations and enter liquidation (https://www.fitchratings.com/research/corporate-finance/fitch-affirms-withdraws-ratings-on-spirit-airlines-places-eetcs-on-rwn-06-05-2026). Counterparties should assess bankruptcy recovery rather than normal operating performance; the historical cash-management balance below includes restricted and pooled debtor cash and does not establish currently available liquidity.

ownership.value: Wholly owned subsidiary of Spirit Aviation Holdings, Inc., a public-reporting holding company. The March 12, 2025 reorganization made the airline a limited liability company beneath that parent; new parent shares and warrants were issued to certain creditors.

distress_signals.summary: Started an immediate orderly wind-down and cancelled all flights. The announcement said additional funding was unavailable and that the business required additional liquidity it could not procure.
The July monthly operating report for Spirit Airlines, LLC reported 76 full-time employees as of August 1, 2026, compared with 9,229 as of September 30, 2025.

payment_behaviour.summary: Spirit announced automatic refunds for flights purchased directly with credit or debit cards. Compensation for bookings paid with vouchers, credits or Free Spirit points would instead be determined later through the bankruptcy process.

Spirit told Reuters that most customers who paid by credit or debit card had been refunded by the evening of May 2, with a small percentage still processing. The company cautioned that refunds could take time to appear in customers' accounts; this was company-reported refund performance, not evidence of normal supplier-payment performance.

debt_events.summary: Spirit Airlines, LLC filed for Chapter 11 protection in the Southern District of New York, case 25-11896. Its case is jointly administered with Spirit Aviation Holdings, Inc. and other affiliates under lead case 25-11897.

Entered a debtor-in-possession credit agreement naming Spirit Airlines, LLC as borrower and certain subsidiaries as guarantors. The facility provided for up to $475 million of aggregate term loans, subject to its terms and funding conditions; this is a historical facility commitment, not a verified current debt or cash balance.

Announced an amendment to the DIP credit agreement providing for a previously agreed $100 million incremental funding round. The announcement said $50 million, less original issue discount, was immediately usable; use of the remainder depended on progress toward a standalone reorganization or strategic transaction.
Additional financing could not be obtained, and Spirit began winding down operations. The company said sustaining the business required additional liquidity it did not have and could not procure.
